analysis: The code snippet parses a string of options separated by spaces. When an option contains a colon, it extracts the key and value using substring. The substring calls are only made when colonLoc != -1, i.e., the colon exists in the option. The first call uses substring(0, colonLoc) where beginIndex=0 and endIndex=colonLoc. Since colonLoc is a non-negative integer less than the length of the string (indexOf returns a valid index), and 0 <= colonLoc <= length (actually colonLoc < length, so colonLoc <= length-1, making endIndex valid). The second call uses substring(colonLoc+1) where beginIndex = colonLoc+1, which is at least 1 and at most length (if colon is at the last character, colonLoc+1 = length, which is allowed as per documentation). Therefore, both calls have valid indices, and the IndexOutOfBoundsException cannot be thrown.
remark: The code ensures that substring is only invoked when the colon is present in the option string. Consequently, the begin and end indices used in the substring calls are always within the valid range (0 <= beginIndex <= length, and endIndex <= length), preventing any IndexOutOfBoundsException.
